title: Audit Console — ad-hoc slices, cursored browsing, CSV/NDJSON dump, and query bookmarks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Customers and ops teams need a fast way to slice audit data in the Console for troubleshooting, compliance, and incident investigations. Current viewer is limited: unpaged full-table loads for complex queries cause timeouts, exports are opaque (single CSV blob), and saved queries are primitive. This ticket implements an ad-hoc slice + cursored browsing UX with NDJSON/CSV dumps (streamed), a lightweight bookmarking feature for queries, and RBAC-v2-aware export controls so admins can constrain downloadable scopes.
scope: In-scope: console UI for building and bookmarking queries; server-side cursored pagination (opaque cursors) for large result sets; streaming export endpoints producing CSV and NDJSON with role-aware row-level filtering; admin policy hooks that surface export permissions; telemetry for export usage. Out-of-scope: long-term cold storage exports (S3), analytics pipelines, or new SIEM connectors (follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Users can page through results with stable opaque cursors that survive short reboots; 2) Exports can be initiated from a query and delivered as streamed NDJSON or CSV with consistent columns; 3) Export endpoints enforce RBAC v2 and honor attribute-based filters (org_id, team_id, resource); 4) Bookmarks (query bookmarks) are storable and editable in the Console and honor sharing ACLs; 5) Performance: paged list responses return first page <350ms for typical cardinalities; streaming export starts pushing first byte <3s for 1M row queries; 6) Unit/integration tests and an e2e smoke test are present; 7) Documentation and a short runbook for admins are added to Confluence.
implementation_notes: API: POST /api/audit/queries/execute returns {items, next_cursor}. GET /api/audit/queries/export?format=ndjson|csv initiates a streaming response; accepts cursor or ad-hoc filter set. Back-end: use existing audit-log shard service (ENG-70112) + a new cursor layer that encodes (shard_id, offset, filter_hash) signed with service key. Streaming pipeline uses small memory footprint iterators and backpressure to avoid OOM. RBAC: consult the RBAC v2 enforcement library (ENG-72220) at request boundary and apply row-level masking for restricted fields. Bookmarks persisted in metadata store with ACLs and versioning. Implement feature flag console.audit_v2.cursor_export behind runtime flag.
security_considerations: Exports are sensitive. Enforce: 1) role-based allowlist for export feature; 2) audit entry created for every export initiation with requestor, filters, and returned bytes; 3) rate limits and size caps per organization; 4) admins can disable exports org-wide via admin controls; 5) SSO/SAML enforcement is validated for bookmark-sharing flows. Security review required before GA.
migration_notes: Existing saved searches migrate to bookmarks with a best-effort mapping. Any saved search referencing legacy column names will be flagged during migration and placed in a 'needs migration' state for manual review.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind console.audit_v2.cursor_export; 2) internal dogfood org for 48h; 3) staged rollout to 10% of orgs with high-traffic sampling and extra telemetry; 4) full rollout after 2 weeks without regressions.
open_questions: - Should exported NDJSON include a metadata header with filter fingerprint? (security asked for it)\n- How to handle row-level encryption keys if customers enable KMS-at-rest?\n- Do we need an admin approval workflow for exports over threshold size?
